title: Netherlands to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
summary: The Dutch government said it will resist US plans to further restrict ASML Holding NV’s sales to China, calling the proposed rules a threat to Europe’s most valuable company and widening a rift with Washington.

title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring
summary: SAP SE is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: FIFA Says Hackers Accessed Personal Data in Cyberattack
summary: FIFA was targeted by a cyberattack that resulted in hackers accessing “personal and business information,” the football governing body said in a statement on Thursday.

title: QRT to Merge $2 Billion Hedge Fund With Flagship Qube Strategy
summary: Qube Research & Technologies, one of the fastest growing investment firms in the world, is set to merge its crypto-focused money pool with its flagship hedge fund strategy.

title: Africa’s Intra-Continental Trade Hit $213.8 Billion But Faces Payment Barriers
summary: The value of trade between African nations rose about 6% last year to $213.8 billion, but accounted for only 14.6% of the continent’s total trade due to regional economic integration challenges, according to a study.

title: StanChart’s Crypto Custody Unit Suffers Data Breach
summary: Standard Chartered’s crypto custody subsidiary Zodia Custody Ltd. said it had suffered a security breach, exposing some client and staff information.

title: TrustedRouter Aims to Give Companies Greater Privacy With AI
summary: The startup offers companies a way to keep employees’ AI use private from model makers

title: Investec Sees Opportunities in Three Key AI Buckets
summary: Jimmy Muchechetere, equity research analyst at Investec, says the AI trade isn't over and there are value opportunities across the spectrum. He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for Funding at $33 Billion Value
summary: ElevenLabs, a company building artificial intelligence voice models and agents, is in early discussions for a funding round at a target valuation of $33 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Marc Levinson on How UPS Created Modern Logistics
summary: UPS was founded nearly a century ago in the basement of a Seattle saloon by James E. Casey and his business partner Claude Ryan. It is now hard to imagine modern, globalized life, and the logistics required to prop it up, without the innovations Casey and his partners at UPS cooked up during the company's early decades. Marc Levinson has just written a biography of Casey and the company he founded — UPS Man: James E. Casey and the Creation of Modern Logistics — which was a lot harder to do than you might imagine, because Casey shunned the spotlight and his contributions were virtually unknown outside of UPS. In today's episode, Levinson tells us why UPS is so secretive about its history, how Casey and his partners helped figure out the last mile problem and popularized parcel delivery, and how scientific management theories influenced everything the company did. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic’s Stock Sparks Divide Inside One Wall Street Firm
summary: Two equity analysts at a single Wall Street research firm have taken the unusual step of posting conflicting views on the outlook for the hottest stock in the market: Anthropic PBC’s newly listed shares.

title: AI Trade Rebounds in Late Buying Ahead of US Holiday
summary: Stocks rose alongside US equity-index futures as investors returned to the artificial intelligence trade in the runup to the Thanksgiving holiday after a week of whipsawing. Bloomberg's Neil Campling has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Banks Risk Outages as They Contend With AI Threats
summary: The risk of cyberattacks is forcing banks to contend with a growing number of technical hiccups as they race to adapt aging infrastructure and find vulnerabilities before they’re exploited. Artificial intelligence is advancing so fast that IT teams patch first and ask questions later, which can risk outages. Speaking to Bloomberg last week, Citigroup Inc. Chief Executive Officer Jane Fraser warned of a “tsunami” of patches. Bella Farr reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Philippine Investors Explore Stablecoins to Buy Retail Bonds
summary: About 1,200 Philippine investors used digital tokens to fund roughly $1 million of retail dollar bond purchases after the Southeast Asian nation opened a new channel for investing in government debt.

title: Malaysia Removes About 40,000 Bullying Posts in Online Crackdown
summary: Malaysia said online platforms removed more than 40,000 pieces of bullying-related content this year at the government’s request, as the Southeast Asian nation steps up efforts to protect children from harmful material on social media.

title: Apple to Expand India Retail Network With New Store in Hyderabad
summary: Apple Inc. is opening a new store in the southern Indian city of Hyderabad next month, continuing a drive to expand its retail network in one of its fastest-growing overseas markets.

title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge
summary: Elon Musk and SpaceX will give every child in the US two shares in the space exploration company, doubling a commitment the world’s richest person made just last month.

title: Xpeng Says Its Humanoid Robot Will Cost the Same as an EV
summary: Xpeng Inc.’s humanoid robots will cost roughly the same as an electric vehicle when they go on sale to the public in the second quarter.

title: Huawei Teases Next-Gen AI Memory Chip to Take On Samsung, Hynix
summary: Huawei Technologies Co. is preparing to release details of a new high-bandwidth memory chip that could potentially surpass current offerings from Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., moving to launch Chinese production of a key AI component currently blocked by US sanctions.

title: Viettel, Singtel Building Subsea Cable for Data-Hungry Vietnam
summary: A consortium led by Viettel Group and Singapore Telecommunications is beginning construction on a submarine cable system in Ho Chi Minh City as Vietnam’s demand for internet bandwidth rapidly grows.
